verdicts.reason: A keeps a sensible top-to-bottom order (product, logo, headline, copy, CTA), but the logo is centred under the product while the text is left-aligned, the CTA is centred and doesn't line up with either, and the legal line is too small to read. B puts the 'Taste the Glow' CTA in the top-left corner above the logo and headline, which breaks the reading order and makes the CTA compete with the brand. B also leaves the CTA-less bottom third as dead space and has the same unreadable legal text.

A is the broken layout from pair 1: the CTA is jammed into the top-left corner ahead of the headline, the order is jumbled and the bottom of the canvas is empty. B follows the original's order: logo top-left, then product, headline, copy, availability and the CTA last on one left axis. Its remaining flaws: the legal line is unreadably small, and the logo and product sit slightly off the text's left edge.

A is again the layout with the CTA first in the top-left corner, which breaks hierarchy and order and leaves the bottom third empty. B's order works (logo, headline, copy, product, CTA), but the headline and body copy run over the olive decorative circle, which lowers their contrast. B also has a large dead gap between 'Now in 4-packs' and the product, and its legal text is microscopic.
